description: We are driven by a simple, restless love for learning. To us, curiosity is a compass—a way to listen to the rhythm of the earth, decode the whispers of the sky, and turn raw science into grounded truth. Every real-world challenge is an invitation to craft solutions that respect both the wisdom of nature and the human heart. We build bridges between curiosity and care, growing better with every line of code, every question asked, and every seed of hope planted for tomorrow.
summary:
Farmers make decisions about water, soil, costs, and weather at the same time, yet few analytical tools turn farm data into clear choices, and small family farms adopt precision technologies far less than large ones. We developed CIDA (Crop Intelligence & Decision Assistant), a clean and intuitive website that helps farmers plan crop rotations with NASA Earth observations.
CIDA reads each field through three factors: water (soil moisture, precipitation, and evapotranspiration), environment (temperature, solar irradiance, and vapor pressure deficit), and soil (slope, elevation, and water retention). Each factor is compared with the same period in previous years and flagged with green, orange, or red alerts that show whether conditions will help or harm the harvest. Using Fuzzy TOPSIS to handle climate uncertainty and balance trade-offs, crops are ranked according to the producer’s priorities, such as saving water. A strategy simulator with a rotation preview then lets the farmer test options before planting, for example adding a crop that fixes nutrients in the soil. Every strategy, including the current rotation, is evaluated on the same criteria.   
Built on Klein’s Recognition-Primed Decision model, CIDA supports the farmer’s judgment with evidence instead of replacing it, helping farms of any size adapt to changing conditions.
details:
Why: Farmers Don’t Lack Satellite Data—They Lack a Decision Architecture 

Farmers do not lack satellite data; they lack a way to turn it into a decision. Every season, growers juggle erratic rain, water scarcity, heat stress, and soil degradation simultaneously, yet most agricultural tools drop raw map layers and leave interpretation entirely to the user. USDA data reveals the multi-variable reality of farming decisions: 64% of fertilizer users decide based on input costs, 44.3% on crop prices, and 41% on weather. Meanwhile, the U.S. GAO warns that very few digital tools translate agricultural data into actionable field choices.

This gap is widest for smallholders. Farms under two hectares represent 5 of every 6 farms on Earth and produce roughly 35% of the world’s food, yet only 13% of small family farms use yield or soil maps (compared to 68% of large operations). Trust is another barrier: 52% of growers in the Iowa Farm Poll worry about the misuse of their farm data.

2. How: Merging Cognitive Science (RPD) with Multi-Sensor NASA Fusion & Fuzzy TOPSIS 

CIDA is built on Gary Klein’s Recognition-Primed Decision (RPD) model—derived from studying experts who make rapid, high-stakes decisions under uncertainty. CIDA mirrors this cognitive workflow in software across three core steps:

  1. Situation Recognition (NASA Cues): The user specifies historical depth (1, 3, 5, or 10 years) to compare current conditions against local norms through monthly time series and standard deviations:
    • Water: NASA POWER precipitation and NASA SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture.
    • Environment: NASA POWER temperature, solar radiation, and vapor pressure deficit (VPD) to quantify heat stress and atmospheric evaporative demand.
    • Soil & Relief: Root-zone moisture, slope (via SRTM), and ground cover. Every cue expands into a monthly history paired with a plain-language explanation of what it means for the field.
  2. Option Evaluation (Priority-Driven Fuzzy TOPSIS): Farmers rate Water, Environment, and Soil priorities in plain terms (from Very Low to Very High). CIDA converts these inputs into triangular fuzzy numbers (l,m,u) and ranks crop options using Fuzzy TOPSIS—evaluating distance to ideal and worst-case scenarios so that no single extreme metric distorts the outcome. Crop profiles draw from FAO EcoCrop and custom user parameters, backed by an inspectable audit panel for full math transparency.
  3. Mental Simulation (Multi-Crop Rotation & Soil Simulator): Farmers chain 1 to 3 crops to simulate climate fit, soil nutrient carryover, and expected yield. Rules are fully transparent: legumes add residual nitrogen for subsequent grasses, repeating plant families escalates pest and nematode pressure, cycles are matched against regional NASA windows, and baselines are calibrated from the farmer's personal harvest logs. Users can also drag RPD cognitive blocks into the simulation to weigh specific goals like water conservation.
    Additionally, the "My Crops" tracker logs real harvests to feed both the simulator and personal yield/profit forecasts.

Why CIDA Is Creative

  • Decision Architecture, Not a Dashboard: Combines cognitive science (RPD), NASA time series, and fuzzy multi-criteria ranking into a single cohesive workflow.
  • Mirrors Expert Thought: Organizes evidence the way an experienced grower thinks: cues first, options second, and "what-if" simulations third.
  • Transparency by Design: Visible model rules, an inspectable Fuzzy TOPSIS audit trail, and explicit uncertainty handling.
  • Farmer-Centered: Driven by grower priorities, custom crop profiles, and real harvest history.

Tech Stack & Architecture

  • NASA Data Integration: Multi-sensor Earth observations from NASA POWER (agroclimatology), SMAP L4 (root-zone soil moisture & soil physics), GPM IMERG (precipitation), GLDAS (land assimilation), MODIS NDVI (vegetation vigor), and SRTM (terrain elevation & slope), accessed programmatically via earthaccess (NASA Earthdata) and REST APIs.
  • Backend: Python (FastAPI, Uvicorn, xarray, h5netcdf, h5py, pandas, numpy, scipy).
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Chart.js, deployed on Vercel.
  • Authentication & Storage: Supabase with Row-Level Security (RLS) for secure user accounts, farm records, and harvest logs.
  • AI & Agronomy: Paired with Claude Sonnet for architecture and debugging; grounded in FAO EcoCrop, EMBRAPA rotation guidelines, and NASA telemetry.

3. Impact: Accessible Precision Agronomy Built for Real-World Resilience 

We intend to put institutional-grade NASA telemetry directly into the hands of small and medium family farms. By making the benefits of nitrogen fixation, soil cover, and water-smart crop sequencing visible prior to planting, CIDA helps growers cut unnecessary irrigation and fertilizer costs, curb erosion on sloped terrain, and build long-term climate resilience.
